haiku-low.q1: Two of three probe sites seeing three consecutive failures of A's /healthz, 10 s apart. Detection alone only pages on-call and changes nothing.
haiku-low.q2: It stops before any change unless the person passes the explicit accept-data-loss override. Only then does it go on to fence A.
haiku-low.q3: B's database is promoted only after A is fenced. B's workers start only after jobs are reset. DNS moves only after B's app passes its health check.
haiku-low.q4: Sessions are not replicated, so B's Redis holds no sessions from A. Users sign in again.
haiku-low.q5: It is never reused as primary. When A returns, it is rebuilt as a replica of B. Moving back is a separate planned switchover.
haiku-low.q6: NOT STATED. The fencing mechanism is not chosen yet, and app-level fencing alone does not stop a partitioned A whose database still accepts connections.
haiku-low.q7: The control store, whose location is still open. It holds the active region and run progress. Which other parts write or read it is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Jobs still marked running are set back to queued so B's workers can pick them up. Some work may run again, so jobs must be idempotent.
haiku-low.q9: Resume from the last logged step once the cause is fixed, or abort. Abort undoes nothing. Going back to A is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q10: Its cached DNS keeps A's address for up to about a minute, given the 60 s TTL. Nothing further about its experience is stated.
haiku-low.q11: Work A did after the last replicated change is lost. The target is 30 s, and replay lag is typically under 5 s. Lag over 30 s stops the run unless overridden.

sonnet.q1: On-call running the failover command starts it. Detection (2 of 3 probe sites see 3 consecutive /healthz failures, 10 s apart) only pages on-call; nothing else happens automatically.
sonnet.q2: If B's recorded replay lag is over 30 s, the command stops with nothing changed (A not fenced) unless the person passes the explicit accept-data-loss override; with the override it continues to fencing.
sonnet.q3: Before promotion: A must be fenced (the lag check passed or was overridden first). Before workers start: B is promoted/writable and jobs left running are reset to queued. Before DNS moves: B's app is scaled up and passes its health check.
sonnet.q4: Sessions are lost: B's Redis holds no sessions from A (not replicated), so users must sign in again.
sonnet.q5: It is never reused as primary. When A returns, it is rebuilt as a replica of B.
sonnet.q6: NOT STATED. Fencing is required to work even when A is unreachable, but the mechanism is an open question and not yet chosen; apps can respect a fence, but that alone doesn't stop a partitioned A whose database accepts connections. If fencing can't be confirmed, B is not promoted.
sonnet.q7: The control store holds the active-region record (and failover run progress), but its location is an open question. The command takes the failover lock and keeps A as active until the switch completes. Which other parts read it is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q8: Jobs still marked running (no worker) are set back to queued by the command after B is promoted and before B's workers start, so B's workers pick them up. Work after the last replicated change is lost (within RPO), and some work may rerun, so jobs must be idempotent.
sonnet.q9: The run stops at its last logged step; once the cause is fixed the person can resume from that step, or abort. Abort does not un-fence A or un-promote B. Going back to A: NOT STATED as a failover option; moving back is a separate, planned switchover, with A rebuilt as a replica of B (no automatic failback). Before fencing/promotion (e.g. lag stop) A is untouched.
sonnet.q10: The record has a 60 s TTL, so such clients may keep A's address for up to about a minute. What they experience beyond that (e.g. errors or timeouts against fenced A) is NOT STATED explicitly; after the TTL expires they reach B.
sonnet.q11: Up to the replica's replay lag, which is typically under 5 s and trails A by a few seconds; the RPO target is 30 s. The command refuses to proceed (without override) if recorded lag exceeds 30 s. Note the recorded lag stays fixed while A is down, so actual loss beyond it is not captured. Also, work A did after the last replicated change is lost.
